title: Three Hundred Against a Vast Army
overview: God shrinks Gideon's army from thousands to just three hundred men, then uses a night of noise and light to send the invading Midianite army into panic and flight.

parts.label: Too many soldiers (vv. 1-3)
parts.note: Gideon camps by a spring above the huge Midianite camp, but God says his army is too big, because Israel would credit its own strength for the win. Under an old rule letting frightened men go home before battle, 22,000 leave and 10,000 remain.

parts.label: The test at the water (vv. 4-8)
parts.note: Only the 300 who scoop water to their mouths and lap it are kept, while those who kneel to drink go home. Interpreters are unsure why this test was chosen; some see alert, ready men, others think the point is simply to leave the smallest group.

parts.label: A dream in the enemy camp (vv. 9-15)
parts.note: God tells Gideon to attack, adding that if he is afraid he can first sneak down with his servant Purah, and there he overhears a soldier's dream of a barley loaf flattening a tent. Barley bread was cheap food of the poor, so the loaf likely stands for humble Israel toppling the invaders, and Gideon worships and rouses his men.

parts.label: Trumpets, jars and torches (vv. 16-22)
parts.note: In three groups around the camp, the men strike just after the guard changes, smashing clay jars to reveal hidden torches, blowing trumpets and shouting. The sleeping Midianites, probably thinking a huge force surrounds them, turn their swords on each other and flee, which the text credits to the LORD.

parts.label: The chase to the Jordan (vv. 23-25)
parts.note: Men from several tribes join the chase, and the tribe of Ephraim seizes the river crossings to block the escape. They kill two Midianite commanders, Oreb ("raven") and Zeeb ("wolf"), and bring their heads to Gideon, a brutal detail the story reports without comment.

think: When something goes well in your life, how do you decide how much of the credit belongs to you and how much to things beyond your control?
